```{r load}
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)

vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
v <- readRDS(vd("monthly_values.rds"))
prov <- v$provenance
daily <- readRDS(vd("station_daily.rds"))
lh <- utils::read.csv(vd("life_history_bulk.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
map <- readRDS(vd("monthly_map.rds"))

# every value below is the published product's, each checked against what it
# was built from by data-raw/monthly_vignette_data.R: none may differ
stopifnot(identical(prov$published$manifest, wet:::wet_catalog_url), all(prov$published_check$compared > 0),
          all(prov$published_check$differing == 0))

# colours come from the gq registry, so no hex literal appears in this
# vignette; assert the class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_segment.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_st <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_station.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_main <- gq::gq_reg_main()
classes <- function(r, layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(r$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_src <- classes(reg, "flow_source", c("observed", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"))
pal_hydro <- classes(reg_st, "hydrograph", c("band", "median", "window"))
pal_map <- classes(reg, "bulkley_map", c("catchment_quick", "catchment_houston", "catchment_buck", "stream_main",
                                         "station"))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pct <- function(x) paste0(ifelse(round(x) > 0, "+", ""), round(x), "%")
and_text <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
to_title <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), " "), function(w) {
    big <- !w %in% c("at", "the", "near", "of")
    w[big] <- paste0(toupper(substring(w[big], 1, 1)), substring(w[big], 2))
    paste(w, collapse = " ")
  }, "")
}
# stopifnot(logical(0)) passes, so a lookup that can come back empty is checked
one <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1, !is.na(x))
  x
}
days <- c(365.25, wet_month_days())
base <- 1981:2010
base_text <- paste0(min(base), "–", max(base))
period_of <- function(src) unique(v$segments$period[v$segments$source == src])
# the product spells a period with a hyphen; the prose with an en dash. The
# prose says both sources cover the gauges' period
stopifnot(identical(period_of("wet_balance"), paste0(min(base), "-", max(base))),
          identical(period_of("pcic_routed"), period_of("wet_balance")))
```

The R package [`wet`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet) publishes a
mean flow for every stream segment in BC's Freshwater Atlas: one for the year
and one for each month, from two sources (`vignette("segment-discharge")`).
This article is about the months. It shows how to read them for one stream,
sets them against the gauge record and the Chinook windows on the Bulkley
River, and scores them at the gauges the water balance is built on.

## What a month holds

```{r months}
sg <- v$segments
stations <- c("08EE013", "08EE003", "08EE004")
names_st <- c(stats::setNames(attr(daily, "provenance")$stations$station_name,
                              attr(daily, "provenance")$stations$station_number),
              stats::setNames(unique(v$gauges[c("station_number", "station_name")])$station_name,
                              unique(v$gauges[c("station_number", "station_name")])$station_number))
st_label <- stats::setNames(sprintf("%s (%s)", to_title(names_st[stations]), stations), stations)

# routed month 0 is the plain mean of its twelve months; weighted by days it
# differs by this much on the Bulkley segments
r <- sg[sg$source == "pcic_routed", ]
wtd <- vapply(stations, function(s) {
  q <- r$q_m3s[r$station_number == s & r$month > 0][order(r$month[r$station_number == s & r$month > 0])]
  sum(q * days[-1]) / sum(days[-1])
}, 0)
plain <- r$q_m3s[r$month == 0][match(stations, r$station_number[r$month == 0])]
wtd_diff <- max(abs(100 * (plain / wtd - 1)))
# the prose: the balance's months add up to its month 0, routed's do not
bal <- sg[sg$source == "wet_balance", ]
bal_sum <- vapply(stations, function(s) {
  x <- bal[bal$station_number == s & bal$month > 0, ]
  sum(x$q_m3s * days[x$month + 1]) / sum(days[-1])
}, 0)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(bal_sum), bal$q_m3s[bal$month == 0][match(stations, bal$station_number[bal$month == 0])])),
          wtd_diff > 0)
```

Each source fills the twelve months its own way:

- **Routed PCIC** (`pcic_routed`) is the mean of each month's daily flow over
  `r base_text` in PCIC's routed model, placed on FWA segments by
  [`fwapg`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg). Its annual value is
  the plain mean of the twelve months; weighting them by their days would move
  it by at most `r sprintf("%.1f%%", wtd_diff)` on the segments below.
- **The water balance** (`wet_balance`) is the annual flow over `r base_text`,
  split into months by the shares of the year carried by the five gauges most
  like the place (`wet_share_fit()`). Its months add up to its annual value
  exactly.

Neither is the gauge record.

## Reading a segment's twelve months

The parts are public and the manifest names them. One stream is one
`linear_feature_id`; naming its watershed group as well lets
[`duckdb`](https://duckdb.org/) skip the rest, so the read takes seconds.

```{r read, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(wet)
# Buck Creek at its mouth, where gauge 08EE013 sits
q <- wet_segment_monthly(NULL, 17094080, groups = "BULK")

# twelve months a column per source
reshape(q[q$month > 0, c("source", "month", "q_m3s")], idvar = "month",
        timevar = "source", direction = "wide")
```

`wet_segment_monthly()` reads the parts through `duckdb`, or the
[PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) table `wet_db_load()` writes when it
is given a connection. It returns `linear_feature_id, month, q_m3s, source`,
the shape of `wet_station_monthly()`'s gauge record, so a comparison is a join
on `month`. A segment a source lacks comes back with `NA` months, not missing
rows.

## The Bulkley at three gauges

```{r bulkley}
stopifnot(identical(unique(sg$linear_feature_id[sg$station_number == "08EE013"]), 17094080L))
ch <- lh[lh$species_code == "CH" & lh$life_stage %in% c("migration", "spawning", "fry_migration"), ]
stopifnot(nrow(ch) == 3, all(ch$end > ch$start))  # none crosses the new year
stage <- sub("_", " ", ch$life_stage)
windows <- data.frame(window = paste0(toupper(substring(stage, 1, 1)), substring(stage, 2)),
                      start = ch$start, end = ch$end)
md_text <- function(md) {
  d <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", md))
  paste(format(d, "%b"), as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}

# observed monthly means, 1981-2010: the calibration record (complete years)
# where the gauge is a calibration gauge, otherwise the daily record's
# month-years with at least 20 days of flow, in months that have 10 of them
g <- v$gauges
obs_cal <- g[g$station_number %in% stations & g$month > 0, ]
obs_cal$q_m3s <- obs_cal$obs_mm * obs_cal$area_km2 * 1e6 / (days[obs_cal$month + 1] * 86400 * 1000)
obs_cal$n_years <- obs_cal$n_years
min_days <- 20
min_years <- 10
dh <- daily[daily$source == "hydat", ]
dh$year <- as.integer(format(dh$date, "%Y"))
dh$month <- as.integer(format(dh$date, "%m"))
dh <- dh[dh$year %in% base, ]
my <- stats::aggregate(q_m3s ~ station_number + year + month, dh, function(q) c(mean = mean(q), n = length(q)))
my <- data.frame(my[c("station_number", "year", "month")], q = my$q_m3s[, "mean"], n = my$q_m3s[, "n"])
my <- my[my$n >= min_days, ]
obs_daily <- stats::aggregate(q ~ station_number + month, my, function(q) c(mean = mean(q), n = length(q)))
obs_daily <- data.frame(obs_daily[c("station_number", "month")], q_m3s = obs_daily$q[, "mean"],
                        n_years = obs_daily$q[, "n"])
obs_daily <- obs_daily[obs_daily$n_years >= min_years, ]
not_cal <- setdiff(stations, unique(g$station_number))
stopifnot(identical(not_cal, "08EE003"))
obs <- rbind(obs_cal[c("station_number", "month", "q_m3s", "n_years")],
             obs_daily[obs_daily$station_number %in% not_cal, ])
obs$source <- "observed"
# 08EE003 is seasonal: the months it has, and the years they come from
m003 <- sort(obs$month[obs$station_number == "08EE003"])
stopifnot(identical(m003, min(m003):max(m003)))
m003_text <- paste0(month.name[min(m003)], "–", month.name[max(m003)])
n003 <- length(unique(my$year[my$station_number == "08EE003" & my$month %in% m003]))
# the prose: 08EE003 has no complete year in 1981-2010 (every month with 20 days)
stopifnot(!any(table(my$year[my$station_number == "08EE003"]) == 12))

mid <- function(m) as.Date(sprintf("2001-%02d-15", m))
hyd <- rbind(sg[sg$month > 0, c("station_number", "month", "q_m3s", "source")],
             obs[c("station_number", "month", "q_m3s", "source")])
hyd$date <- mid(hyd$month)
hyd$source <- factor(hyd$source, names(pal_src$values))
hyd$station_number <- factor(hyd$station_number, stations, st_label[stations])

# the windows as strips under each panel, one row each
top <- stats::aggregate(q_m3s ~ station_number, hyd, max)
strip <- merge(top, data.frame(window = windows$window, row = seq_len(nrow(windows)),
                               start = as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$start)),
                               end = as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$end))), by = NULL)
strip$y <- -strip$q_m3s * (0.04 + 0.07 * (strip$row - 1)) - strip$q_m3s * 0.03
strip$h <- strip$q_m3s * 0.045
strip$label_x <- strip$end + 4

peak_month <- function(src) {
  x <- hyd[hyd$station_number == st_label[["08EE013"]] & hyd$source == src, ]
  one(x$month[which.max(x$q_m3s)])
}
stopifnot(peak_month("observed") == 5, peak_month("pcic_routed") == 5)
```

```{r map-data}
# `[` keeps an sf object's geometry only once sf's methods are registered,
# and nothing above has loaded sf
invisible(loadNamespace("sf"))
# the three catchments nest: Buck Creek's inside Houston's, both inside
# Quick's, so they are drawn largest first, each over the one before
catch <- map$catchments
part_of <- c("08EE004" = "catchment_quick", "08EE003" = "catchment_houston", "08EE013" = "catchment_buck")
catch$part <- part_of[catch$station_number]
stopifnot(!anyNA(catch$part))
catch <- catch[match(names(part_of), catch$station_number), ]
inside <- function(a, b) {
  as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_intersection(sf::st_geometry(catch[catch$part == a, ]),
                                            sf::st_geometry(catch[catch$part == b, ])))) /
    as.numeric(sf::st_area(catch[catch$part == a, ]))
}
stopifnot(inside("catchment_buck", "catchment_houston") > 0.99, inside("catchment_houston", "catchment_quick") > 0.99)
area_of <- function(s) format(round(one(catch$area_km2[catch$station_number == s])), big.mark = ",")
# the prose: the gauges' areas here are the fit's (wet's accumulated upstream
# area), within 10% of the FWA catchments drawn
a_fit <- stats::setNames(g$area_km2[match(c("08EE013", "08EE004"), g$station_number)], c("08EE013", "08EE004"))
stopifnot(all(abs(a_fit / catch$area_km2[match(names(a_fit), catch$station_number)] - 1) < 0.1))

map_w <- 7
map_h <- 6
bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_union(catch), 3000))
# room below the catchments for the legend and scale bar
bb[["ymin"]] <- bb[["ymin"]] - 0.2 * (bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]])
bb <- gq::gq_bbox_aspect(bb, asp = map_w / map_h)
lim_x <- c(bb[["xmin"]], bb[["xmax"]])
lim_y <- c(bb[["ymin"]], bb[["ymax"]])
dx <- diff(lim_x)
dy <- diff(lim_y)

st <- map$stations
xy <- sf::st_coordinates(st)
# the Houston gauge sits just west of Buck Creek's mouth: its label goes up
# and to the left, the other two to the right
left <- st$station_number == "08EE003"
st_lab <- data.frame(x = xy[, 1] + ifelse(left, -0.012, 0.012) * dx, y = xy[, 2] + ifelse(left, 0.035, 0) * dy,
                     label = st_label[st$station_number], hjust = ifelse(left, 1, 0))
pl <- sf::st_coordinates(map$places)
pl_lab <- data.frame(x = pl[, 1], y = pl[, 2] - 0.03 * dy, label = map$places$name)

stream_sty <- reg_main$layers$streams_all$classification$classes$WA24111110
lake_sty <- reg_main$layers$lake
town_sty <- reg_main$layers$town
main_streams <- map$streams[map$streams$main, ]

# scale bar in the lower right, its length from gq
sb_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb))
sb <- data.frame(x = lim_x[2] - 0.05 * dx - sb_km * 1000, y = lim_y[1] + 0.05 * dy)
sb$xend <- sb$x + sb_km * 1000

# keymap: BC with the map extent, in the upper right
key <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = map$bc, fill = "white", colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]], linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = sf::st_as_sfc(bb), fill = NA, colour = pal_map$values[["station"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]],
                                        linewidth = 0.3))
key_w <- 0.22 * dx
key_h <- key_w * 1.05

cap_map <- sprintf(paste(
  "The three gauges and the land each one drains: Buck Creek at its mouth (%s km²), the Bulkley at Houston",
  "just downstream (%s km²), and the Bulkley at Quick (%s km²), which drains both."
), area_of("08EE013"), area_of("08EE003"), area_of("08EE004"))
```

Three gauges, one inside the next. Buck Creek joins the Bulkley at Houston; the
Houston gauge sits just downstream and measures it too, and the Quick gauge,
further down, drains the whole basin above. Buck Creek and Quick are among the
gauges the water balance is built on. Houston is not: it reads only in open
water and has no complete year in `r base_text`.

```{r map, fig.width = map_w, fig.height = map_h, fig.cap = cap_map}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = catch, aes(fill = part), colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]], linewidth = 0.25,
          key_glyph = "rect") +
  geom_sf(data = map$lakes, fill = lake_sty$fill$color, colour = lake_sty$stroke$color,
          linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = map$streams[!map$streams$main, ], colour = stream_sty$color, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = main_streams, aes(colour = "stream_main"), linewidth = 0.8, key_glyph = "path") +
  geom_label(data = pl_lab, aes(x, y, label = label), colour = town_sty$label$color,
             fontface = "bold", size = 3.4, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85,
             label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt")) +
  geom_sf(data = st, aes(shape = "station"), fill = pal_map$values[["station"]], colour = "black",
          size = 3, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_label(data = st_lab, aes(x, y, label = label, hjust = hjust), size = 3.2,
             linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt")) +
  geom_segment(data = sb, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sb, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y, label = paste(sb_km, "km")),
            vjust = -0.7, size = 3.2) +
  # the keymap takes the upper left, which the basin leaves empty; the
  # gauge labels run to the right along the top
  annotation_custom(ggplotGrob(key), xmin = lim_x[1] + 0.02 * dx, xmax = lim_x[1] + key_w + 0.02 * dx,
                    ymin = lim_y[2] - key_h - 0.02 * dy, ymax = lim_y[2] - 0.02 * dy) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_map$values[part_of], labels = pal_map$labels[part_of],

  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_map$values["stream_main"], labels = pal_map$labels["stream_main"],

  guides(shape = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(fill = pal_map$values[["station"]])),

  coord_sf(xlim = lim_x, ylim = lim_y, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.02, 0.02),
        legend.justification = c(0, 0), legend.box.just = "left", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        legend.margin = margin(4, 6, 4, 6), legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt"),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]]))
```

```{r hydrographs, fig.height = 7.2, fig.cap = cap_hyd}
ggplot(hyd) +
  geom_rect(data = strip, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = y - h / 2, ymax = y + h / 2),
            fill = pal_hydro$values[["window"]]) +
  geom_text(data = strip, aes(x = label_x, y = y, label = window), hjust = 0, size = 2.6, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_line(aes(date, q_m3s, colour = source), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(date, q_m3s, colour = source), size = 1.2) +

  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b",
               limits = as.Date(c("2001-01-01", "2001-12-31")), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  facet_wrap(~station_number, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +

```

```{r bulkley-numbers}
freshet <- function(s, src) {
  x <- hyd[hyd$station_number == st_label[[s]] & hyd$source == src & hyd$month %in% 5:6, ]
  sum(x$q_m3s * days[x$month + 1]) / sum(days[x$month + 1])
}
fr <- vapply(c("observed", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"), function(src) freshet("08EE013", src), 0)
fr_q <- vapply(c("observed", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"), function(src) freshet("08EE004", src), 0)
hq <- function(s, src, mo) {
  x <- hyd[hyd$station_number == st_label[[s]] & hyd$source == src & hyd$month %in% mo, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == length(mo))
  x$q_m3s[match(mo, x$month)]
}
# the prose: at both calibration gauges the balance's months are the gauge's
# own monthly pattern (its nearest donor is itself) at the balance's annual
# flow, so every month is off by about the annual's error, and below the gauge;
# routed overshoots Buck Creek's freshet, and at Quick is above the gauge in
# July and August and short of it in May-June by a fifth to a third
ratio_of <- function(s) hq(s, "wet_balance", 1:12) / hq(s, "observed", 1:12)
wb_off <- vapply(c("08EE013", "08EE004"), function(s) 100 * (stats::median(ratio_of(s)) - 1), 0)
stopifnot(identical(prov$share_method, "donor"),
          all(vapply(c("08EE013", "08EE004"), function(s) diff(range(ratio_of(s))) < 0.02, NA)),
          all(wb_off < 0), all(wb_off > -15),
          peak_month("wet_balance") == peak_month("observed"),
          all(hq("08EE004", "pcic_routed", 7:8) > hq("08EE004", "observed", 7:8)),
          fr[["pcic_routed"]] > fr[["observed"]], hq("08EE013", "pcic_routed", 5) > hq("08EE013", "observed", 5))
q_short <- 100 * (fr_q[["pcic_routed"]] / fr_q[["observed"]] - 1)
stopifnot(q_short < -20, q_short > -33)
```

Buck Creek peaks in May, and so does routed PCIC, which overshoots it: its
May–June flow is `r round(fr[["pcic_routed"]], 1)` m³/s against
`r round(fr[["observed"]], 1)` at the gauge. At Quick, routed PCIC is about a
quarter short in May–June (`r round(fr_q[["pcic_routed"]])` m³/s against
`r round(fr_q[["observed"]])`) and high in July and August.

At Buck Creek and Quick the balance's published months are in-sample: the
gauge most like each of them is itself, so the balance there has the gauge's
own monthly pattern at the balance's annual flow, about `r pct(wb_off[["08EE013"]])`
and `r pct(wb_off[["08EE004"]])` in every month. The scores further down hold
each gauge out instead. At Houston the balance is a true estimate for an
ungauged site, and the gauge can check it only in open water.

## Flow in the Chinook windows

```{r windows}
# the gauge's daily record, as the station-flow article reads it: the mean
# over each window, in each 1981-2010 year with enough of the window's days
ws <- wet_window_stats(dh[dh$station_number %in% c("08EE013", "08EE003"), c("station_number", "date", "q_m3s")],
                       windows, stats = "mean")
# a window's mean from monthly means, wet_flow_window(): each day takes its
# month's mean. The sources' months once per gauge; the observed months per
# window, since each window has its own years
src_w <- wet_flow_window(sg[sg$station_number %in% c("08EE013", "08EE003"), c("station_number", "source", "month", "q_m3s")],
                         windows, by = c("station_number", "source"))
stopifnot(all(src_w$basis == "monthly"))
src_q <- function(s, src, w) src_w$q_m3s[src_w$station_number == s & src_w$source == src & src_w$window == w]
# the same windows from the published days (segment_daily), the same call
sd <- v$segments_daily
src_d <- wet_flow_window(sd[sd$station_number %in% c("08EE013", "08EE003"), c("station_number", "source", "doy", "q_m3s")],
                         windows, by = c("station_number", "source"))
stopifnot(all(src_d$basis == "daily"))
src_qd <- function(s, src, w) src_d$q_m3s[src_d$station_number == s & src_d$source == src & src_d$window == w]
win <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("08EE013", "08EE003"), function(s) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(windows)), function(k) {
    w <- windows[k, ]
    yrs <- ws$year[ws$station_number == s & ws$period == w$window]
    # the observed months over the same years as the daily means
    mo <- my[my$station_number == s & my$year %in% yrs, ]
    om <- stats::aggregate(q ~ month, mo, mean)
    obs_w <- wet_flow_window(data.frame(month = om$month, q_m3s = om$q), w, by = character())
    data.frame(station_number = s, window = w$window, span = paste(md_text(w$start), "–", md_text(w$end)),
               years = length(yrs),
               daily = mean(ws$value[ws$station_number == s & ws$period == w$window]),
               obs_months = obs_w$q_m3s,
               routed = src_q(s, "pcic_routed", w$window),
               balance = src_q(s, "wet_balance", w$window),
               routed_daily = src_qd(s, "pcic_routed", w$window),
               balance_daily = src_qd(s, "wet_balance", w$window))
  }))
}))
stopifnot(!anyNA(win), all(win$years >= min_years))
approx_err <- 100 * (win$obs_months / win$daily - 1)
err_of <- function(col) 100 * (win[[col]] / win$daily - 1)
# what the days do to a window: each source's move from its months to its
# days, beside the gauge's own move from its monthly means to its daily record
move_of <- function(src) 100 * (win[[paste0(src, "_daily")]] / win[[src]] - 1)
win$move_obs <- 100 * (win$daily / win$obs_months - 1)
win$move_routed <- move_of("routed")
win$move_balance <- move_of("balance")
# the approximation per window, at its worse gauge
approx_w <- tapply(abs(approx_err), win$window, max)[windows$window]
good_w <- names(approx_w)[approx_w < 5]
poor_w <- names(approx_w)[approx_w >= 5]
in_poor <- win$window %in% poor_w
at <- function(s, w = poor_w) win$station_number == s & win$window %in% w
wp <- function(col, s) one(win[[col]][at(s)])
ep <- function(col, s) one(err_of(col)[at(s)])
# a move the prose calls a fall is printed unsigned, and must be negative
drop_of <- function(col, s) {
  x <- wp(col, s)
  stopifnot(x < 0)
  sprintf("%.0f%%", -x)
}
# the reason the prose gives for the poor window: the second half of July
# runs well below July's mean
late_july <- vapply(c("08EE013", "08EE003"), function(st) {
  x <- dh[dh$station_number == st & dh$month == 7, ]
  mean(x$q_m3s[as.integer(format(x$date, "%d")) >= 15]) / mean(x$q_m3s)
}, 0)
# the prose, sentence by sentence. Good windows: the gauge's daily record and
# its monthly means agree within 5%, and the days move no source's window by
# more than a tenth. The poor window is fry migration alone, and there the
# monthly means overstate the gauge by about a quarter at both gauges. Routed
# PCIC's days fall faster than the gauge's, and its error shrinks at both. The
# balance's days at Buck Creek fall as the gauge's do (its donor is itself),
# leaving its annual error; at Houston they fall less than half as far, and
# the balance stays several times the gauge in both late-summer windows
late_w <- c("Spawning", "Fry migration")
b003 <- err_of("balance_daily")[win$station_number == "08EE003" & win$window %in% late_w]
stopifnot(identical(poor_w, "Fry migration"), all(late_july < 0.9),
          max(approx_w[good_w]) < 5, all(abs(c(win$move_routed, win$move_balance)[!in_poor]) < 10),
          all(approx_err[in_poor] > 20), all(approx_err[in_poor] < 30),
          all(win$move_routed[in_poor] < win$move_obs[in_poor]),
          all(abs(err_of("routed_daily")[in_poor]) < abs(err_of("routed")[in_poor])),
          abs(wp("move_balance", "08EE013") - wp("move_obs", "08EE013")) < 1,
          abs(ep("balance_daily", "08EE013") - wb_off[["08EE013"]]) < 2,
          wp("move_balance", "08EE003") < 0,
          abs(wp("move_balance", "08EE003")) < abs(wp("move_obs", "08EE003")) / 2,
          length(b003) == 2, all(b003 > 200))
```

The windows start and end mid-month, and a window taken from monthly means
gives every day its month's mean. Where flow changes slowly within the month
that is fine: in `r tolower(and_text(good_w))` the gauge's daily record and its
own monthly means agree within `r sprintf("%.0f%%", max(approx_w[good_w]))`.
`r and_text(poor_w)` takes the second half of July, when the freshet is
receding, and there the monthly means overstate the gauge by about a quarter.

The published days fix that wherever a source's daily pattern is right. Routed
PCIC's days fall through late July faster than the gauge's, and its
fry-migration error shrinks at both gauges. The balance's days follow a pattern
borrowed from the gauges most like the place. At Buck Creek that is Buck Creek
itself, so its days fall with the gauge's (`r drop_of("move_balance", "08EE013")`,
against the gauge's `r drop_of("move_obs", "08EE013")`) and only its annual
error remains. At Houston the borrowed pattern keeps more water into late
summer: its days fall only `r drop_of("move_balance", "08EE003")`, and the
balance stays several times the gauge in both late-summer windows. That error
is ours. The table has the numbers.

```{r window-table}
tab <- data.frame(
  Gauge = st_label[win$station_number], Window = paste0(win$window, " (", win$span, ")"),
  Years = win$years,
  `Daily record` = sprintf("%.1f", win$daily),
  `Monthly, day-weighted` = sprintf("%.1f", win$obs_months),
  `Routed PCIC (months)` = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", win$routed, pct(err_of("routed"))),
  `Routed PCIC (days)` = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", win$routed_daily, pct(err_of("routed_daily"))),
  `Water balance (months)` = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", win$balance, pct(err_of("balance"))),
  `Water balance (days)` = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", win$balance_daily, pct(err_of("balance_daily"))),
  check.names = FALSE
)
tab$Gauge[duplicated(tab$Gauge)] <- ""
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrrrrr",
             caption = paste0("Mean flow (m³/s) in each Chinook window, ", base_text, ". Daily record: the gauge's ",
                              "own daily flow, averaged over the window in each year with enough of its days. Monthly, ",
                              "day-weighted: the same years' observed monthly means with every day given its month's ",
                              "mean, which is how a window is read from monthly values. Each source twice: from its ",
                              "published months, read the same way, and from its published days. In brackets, the ",
                              "difference from the daily record."))
```

## Monthly error at the gauges

```{r scores}
a <- g[g$month == 0, ]
# a gauge whose segment carries under this share of its observed flow is left
# out of routed's scores, as the routed report leaves it out
# (scripts/pcic_routed_lib.R, routed_far_low)
far_low <- 0.2
far <- a$station_number[!is.na(a$routed_mm) & a$routed_mm < far_low * a$obs_mm]
n_routed <- sum(!is.na(a$routed_mm))
m <- g[g$month > 0, ]
# modelled over observed: a zero month is a ratio of 0 (an error of -100%),
# which ranks like any other, so the medians keep it
m$ratio_wb <- m$wb_mm / m$obs_mm
m$ratio_r <- m$routed_mm / m$obs_mm
# each source on all its own gauges, every month: no observed month is zero,
# so every ratio is defined. The balance at every calibration gauge; routed
# where its segment has flow, less the far-low ones. Restricting the balance
# to routed's gauges would move it (it reads low in winter where routed is absent)
stopifnot(all(m$obs_mm > 0), !anyNA(m$ratio_wb))
bal <- m
both <- m[!is.na(m$routed_mm) & !m$station_number %in% far, ]
n_bal_gauges <- length(unique(bal$station_number))
n_both_gauges <- length(unique(both$station_number))
n_zero_wb <- sum(bal$wb_mm <= 0)
stopifnot(n_zero_wb == 0, 12 * n_both_gauges == nrow(both), n_routed - length(far) == n_both_gauges,
          12 * n_bal_gauges == nrow(bal), !anyNA(both$ratio_r))
band <- 0.2
summ <- function(d, col, src) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d[[col]], d$month), function(r) {
    data.frame(source = src, median = 100 * (stats::median(r) - 1),
               q25 = 100 * (stats::quantile(r, 0.25, names = FALSE) - 1),
               q75 = 100 * (stats::quantile(r, 0.75, names = FALSE) - 1),
               within = 100 * mean(abs(r - 1) <= band))
  }))
}
sm <- rbind(cbind(month = 1:12, summ(bal, "ratio_wb", "wet_balance")),
            cbind(month = 1:12, summ(both, "ratio_r", "pcic_routed")))
smv <- function(src, mo, col) {
  x <- sm[[col]][sm$source == src & sm$month %in% mo]
  stopifnot(length(x) == length(mo), !anyNA(x))
  x
}
# head to head on the gauges both sources are scored at
sh <- rbind(cbind(month = 1:12, summ(both, "ratio_wb", "wet_balance")),
            cbind(month = 1:12, summ(both, "ratio_r", "pcic_routed")))
shv <- function(src, mo, col) sh[[col]][sh$source == src & sh$month %in% mo]
# the gauges routed PCIC does not reach, where the balance stands alone
un <- bal[!bal$station_number %in% unique(c(both$station_number, far)), ]
n_un <- length(unique(un$station_number))
n_un_10 <- sum(startsWith(unique(un$station_number), "10"))
un_winter <- vapply(1:3, function(k) 100 * (stats::median(un$ratio_wb[un$month == k]) - 1), 0)
sm$date <- mid(sm$month)
sm$source <- factor(sm$source, names(pal_src$values))

# per-gauge skill on the monthly climatology (wet_flow_validate(), as the
# water-balance report scores it)
sk_wb <- wet_flow_validate(data.frame(station_number = g$station_number, month = g$month,
                                      obs = g$obs_mm, mod = g$wb_mm))
r_ok <- !is.na(g$routed_mm) & !g$station_number %in% far
sk_r <- wet_flow_validate(data.frame(station_number = g$station_number[r_ok], month = g$month[r_ok],
                                     obs = g$obs_mm[r_ok], mod = g$routed_mm[r_ok]))
# each source over its own gauges
nse <- function(sk, col) stats::median(sk$stations[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
cap_err <- paste0(
  "Error in mean monthly flow by month: the median (line) and the middle half of gauges (band), as a ",
  "percentage of the gauge's ", base_text, " mean. The water balance is held out (blocked cross-validation) at ",
  n_bal_gauges, " calibration gauges; routed PCIC at the ", n_both_gauges,
  " of them it covers. Dashed lines mark ±", round(100 * band), "%."
)
```

Monthly flow is scored at the `r n_bal_gauges` gauges the water balance is
built on, against each gauge's monthly means over its complete years in
`r base_text`. The balance is scored **held out**: each gauge's months come
from a fit that never saw it or its neighbours. Routed PCIC is scored on the
segment each gauge snapped to, at the `r n_routed` gauges whose segment has
routed flow, less `r length(far)` where the segment carries under
`r round(100 * far_low)`% of the gauge's flow (a misplaced outlet or snap),
so `r n_both_gauges` gauges.

```{r error-month, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = cap_err}
ggplot(sm, aes(date)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * 100 * band, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75, fill = source), alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median, colour = source), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = median, colour = source), size = 1.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_src$values[-1], labels = pal_src$labels[-1], name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_src$values[-1], labels = pal_src$labels[-1], name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b",
               limits = as.Date(c("2001-01-01", "2001-12-31")), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Error in mean monthly flow")
```

```{r error-table}
et <- data.frame(Month = month.abb,
                 `Balance median` = pct(smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "median")),
                 `Balance within ±20%` = sprintf("%.0f%%", smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "within")),
                 `Routed median` = pct(smv("pcic_routed", 1:12, "median")),
                 `Routed within ±20%` = sprintf("%.0f%%", smv("pcic_routed", 1:12, "within")),
                 check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(et, align = "lrrrr",
             caption = paste0("Median error in mean monthly flow, and the share of gauges within ±",
                              round(100 * band), "% of observed, each source on its own gauges as in the figure above."))
```

```{r score-text}
r_spring <- 3:4
r_summer <- 7:8
# a season's median over its gauge-months, not a mean of monthly medians
season_med <- function(col, mo) 100 * (stats::median(both[[col]][both$month %in% mo]) - 1)
# head to head, on the same gauges
r_closer <- which(shv("pcic_routed", 1:12, "within") > shv("wet_balance", 1:12, "within"))
# the prose: the balance's median is within 10% in every month, highest in
# April, and within the band at fewer than half the gauges in every month;
# routed is low in spring and high in summer
wb_med <- smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "median")
# the freshet at the gauges whose observed flow (not monthly volume) peaks in
# May or June: the balance in the gauge's peak month, against the gauge
bal$obs_q <- bal$obs_mm / days[bal$month + 1]
pk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(bal, bal$station_number), function(x) x[which.max(x$obs_q), ]))
pk <- pk[pk$month %in% 5:6, ]
pk_below <- 100 * mean(pk$ratio_wb < 1)
pk_ratio <- 100 * (stats::median(pk$ratio_wb) - 1)
# the prose names the donor shares and the snow terms they are matched on:
# the fit must have shipped both
stopifnot(identical(prov$share_spec, "snow"), identical(prov$share_method, "donor"))
stopifnot(max(abs(wb_med)) < 10, which.max(wb_med) == 4, pk_below > 50, pk_ratio < 0,
          n_un + n_both_gauges + length(far) == n_bal_gauges, n_un_10 > n_un / 2, all(abs(un_winter) < 10),
          max(smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "within")) < 50,
          all(smv("pcic_routed", r_spring, "median") < -10), all(smv("pcic_routed", r_summer, "median") > 10),
          season_med("ratio_r", r_spring) < -10, season_med("ratio_r", r_summer) > 10,
          length(r_closer) > 0, length(r_closer) < 6)
# per gauge: routed low in spring, high in summer, both
by_g <- function(mo) tapply(both$ratio_r[both$month %in% mo], both$station_number[both$month %in% mo], mean)
g_low <- by_g(r_spring) < 1
g_high <- by_g(r_summer) > 1
stopifnot(identical(names(g_low), names(g_high)), length(g_low) == n_both_gauges)
shape_pct <- 100 * c(low = mean(g_low), high = mean(g_high), both = mean(g_low & g_high))
# the prose: the shape holds at most gauges, not only at the median
stopifnot(shape_pct[["low"]] > 50, shape_pct[["high"]] > 50)
```

The two sources' errors have different shapes.

- **The water balance** is unbiased but imprecise. Its median error is within
  ±10% in every month, highest in April (`r pct(wb_med[4])`), and within ±10%
  in winter too at the `r n_un` gauges routed PCIC does not reach, most of them
  in the Liard. But fewer than half of the gauges fall within
  ±`r round(100 * band)`% in any month. Its months are an annual flow times the
  shares of the year carried by the five gauges most like the place, matched on
  elevation, location and two snow terms (the day half the snowpack has melted
  by, and the peak snow water equivalent). Where the gauge's flow peaks in May
  or June, the balance is below the gauge in that month at `r round(pk_below)`%
  of `r nrow(pk)` gauges, by a median of `r pct(pk_ratio)`. Its median
  Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency, held out, is `r sprintf("%.2f", nse(sk_wb, "nse_month"))`.
  This error is ours.
- **Routed PCIC** has a seasonal shape to its error. It reads low in March and
  April (median `r pct(season_med("ratio_r", r_spring))`) and high in July and
  August (`r pct(season_med("ratio_r", r_summer))`), as if its melt started late
  and ran on; gauge by gauge, low in spring at `r round(shape_pct[["low"]])`%
  of its `r n_both_gauges` gauges and high in summer at
  `r round(shape_pct[["high"]])`%. On the gauges both sources are scored at it
  has more within ±`r round(100 * band)`% than the balance in
  `r length(r_closer)` months of twelve (`r and_text(month.name[r_closer])`).
  Its median efficiency is `r sprintf("%.2f", nse(sk_r, "nse_month"))`. The
  shape is the model's, not the placement's: a misplaced outlet changes one
  gauge's size, and would not move the median of `r n_both_gauges` gauges
  toward a late melt.

```{r groups}
grp <- unique(g[c("station_number", "area_class", "lake")])
grp$lake <- ifelse(grp$lake %in% TRUE, "lake outlet", "not a lake outlet")
grp <- grp[grp$station_number %in% both$station_number, ]
gw <- wet_flow_validate(data.frame(station_number = g$station_number, month = g$month, obs = g$obs_mm,
                                   mod = g$wb_mm)[g$station_number %in% both$station_number, ], grp)$summary
gr <- wet_flow_validate(data.frame(station_number = g$station_number, month = g$month, obs = g$obs_mm,
                                   mod = g$routed_mm)[g$station_number %in% both$station_number, ], grp)$summary
key <- function(s) paste(s$group, s$value)
gt <- data.frame(Group = ifelse(gw$group == "all", "All gauges",
                                ifelse(gw$group == "lake", paste0(toupper(substring(gw$value, 1, 1)),
                                                                  substring(gw$value, 2)),
                                       sub("km2", "km²", gw$value))),
                 Gauges = gw$n,
                 Balance = sprintf("%.2f", gw$nse_month_median),
                 Routed = sprintf("%.2f", gr$nse_month_median[match(key(gw), key(gr))]))
gt <- gt[match(c("all all", paste("area_class", c("<100 km2", "100-1000", "1000-10000", ">10000")),
                 "lake lake outlet", "lake not a lake outlet"), key(gw)), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(gt$Group))
nse_g <- function(s, g, v) one(s$nse_month_median[s$group == g & s$value == v])
# the prose: the balance is the stronger source on basins under 1,000 km2,
# routed on those over it and at lake outlets
small_a <- c("<100 km2", "100-1000")
large_a <- c("1000-10000", ">10000")
stopifnot(all(vapply(small_a, function(k) nse_g(gw, "area_class", k) > nse_g(gr, "area_class", k), NA)),
          all(vapply(large_a, function(k) nse_g(gr, "area_class", k) > nse_g(gw, "area_class", k), NA)),
          nse_g(gr, "lake", "lake outlet") > nse_g(gw, "lake", "lake outlet"),
          nse_g(gw, "lake", "lake outlet") < nse_g(gw, "lake", "not a lake outlet"))
```

By basin size, the balance is the stronger source under 1,000 km² and routed
PCIC above it. Routed PCIC is also the stronger at lake outlets, whose flow a
lake holds back and releases later in the year: routing follows the lake, and
the balance's donor gauges are matched without regard to it.

```{r group-table}
knitr::kable(gt, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrr",
             caption = paste("Median Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of the monthly climatology per gauge,",
                             "by basin size and lake outlets, on the", n_both_gauges, "gauges both sources are scored at."))
```

## Limits

- On a calibration gauge's own segment the published balance is in-sample: the
  gauge's own monthly pattern at the balance's annual flow (two gauges on one
  watershed, 08NM240 and 08NM241, share the mean of theirs). A watershed much
  like a gauge in elevation, location and snow gets almost the same pattern.
  The scores above hold each gauge out instead.
- Houston (08EE003) is seasonal: its monthly means cover `r m003_text`, from
  `r n003` of the years `r base_text`, and its windows rest on the years the
  table gives.
- A window from the published days is right only as far as the source's daily
  pattern is: the balance's is borrowed from gauges (the gauge's own on its own
  segment), routed PCIC's is its model's. The scores above are of the months;
  the daily pattern is scored where it was fitted, not here.
- The scores are province-wide medians by month, split by basin size and lake
  outlets, not by region or season.
- Routed PCIC's annual value is a plain mean of its months, so its months in
  millimetres do not add up to its annual runoff exactly.

## Validation

```{r provenance}
pc <- prov$published_check
stopifnot(identical(prov$shape_method, "donor"), grepl("^[0-9a-f]{32}$", prov$shape_code_md5),
          is.numeric(prov$day_tie), prov$day_tie >= 0,
          length(prov$shape_stations) > 0, all(prov$shape_stations %in% stations))
# the segments whose balance days were made again: those whose watershed
# predictors the copy of the fit held where the data were built (a reduced
# bundle holds the calibration gauges' only; the full run holds every one)
not_held <- setdiff(stations, prov$shape_stations)
held_text <- if (length(not_held) == 0) {
  "on all three segments"
} else {
  paste0("at ", and_text(st_label[prov$shape_stations]), "; the other segment", if (length(not_held) > 1) "s'" else "'s",
         " days rest on the publish report's own check of every day")
}
```

`data-raw/monthly_vignette_data.R` built the data at wet `r prov$wet_commit`
on `r format(prov$built)`, from the published build at wet
`r prov$published$wet_commit` and the water balance fit on HYDAT
`r substr(prov$hydat_release, 1, 10)`. It checked every bundled published value
against what it was built from, and refused to write unless none differed:

```{r provenance-table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Check = pc$check, Compared = format(pc$compared, big.mark = ","),
                        Differing = pc$differing),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             caption = "Published values against their sources.")
```

Routed PCIC's days were routed again from `fwapg`'s sub-basin days and segment
weights, and the balance's days were made again from its published months and
the fit's daily shape `r held_text`; on all three segments each calendar
month's days average to the published month. The held-out monthly balance is
the one the fit stored, and scored again it gives the fit's stored scores. The
values no row above covers rest on the publish report's value-by-value check
of the live build (`` `r prov$published$report` ``).

## Software and citation

```{r citation, results = "asis"}
pkgs <- c("wet", "duckdb", "ggplot2", "gq")
stopifnot(all(vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, NA, quietly = TRUE)))
# the citation record each package ships (inst/CITATION, or its DESCRIPTION),
# written as BibTeX and read back for the line below: the concept DOI where
# the package has one, the version, and the commit when the install recorded
# a full git hash (a build from a checkout records none)
bib <- tempfile(fileext = ".bib")
knitr::write_bib(pkgs, file = bib)
stopifnot(length(readLines(bib)) > 0)
cite_line <- function(p) {
  d <- utils::packageDescription(p)
  ct <- utils::citation(p)
  doi <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(ct), function(i) ct[[i]]$doi))
  doi_text <- if (length(doi)) sprintf(", [doi:%s](https://doi.org/%s)", doi[1], doi[1]) else ""
  sha <- d$RemoteSha
  commit <- if (is.character(sha) && grepl("^[0-9a-f]{40}$", sha)) sprintf(", commit `%s`", substr(sha, 1, 7)) else ""
  sprintf("- `%s` %s%s%s. %s", p, d$Version, doi_text, commit, paste(format(ct[[1]], style = "text"), collapse = " "))
}
cat(vapply(pkgs, cite_line, ""), sep = "\n")
```

Cite `wet` by the DOI above, which resolves to its latest release. How the
balance is built:
[the water balance method](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/research/water_balance_method.md).
